agree.reason: The pace math and the June checkpoint make a believable case, but the ad-background members are never told why ads must stop rather than run alongside membership, and the understated decline weakens the urgency.

honest.reason: The memo honestly softens 'will replace' to a goal and admits a 2027 revenue gap, but it wrongly says the 36% drop took two years when it happened in one, and its $65,000–$70,000 projection for 2027 has no basis in the brief's figures.

works_the_facts.reason: The figures are worked well: $20,352 a year from the pilot, 1.5% of subscribers, 875 members needed, about 13 a week needed against the 35 a week the pilot reached. But it misreads the ad trend, so its 'if nothing changes' case is wrong.

right_comparison.reason: Keeping ads is made to look better than the facts show: a 36% drop in a single year, if it continued, would leave about $54,000 in 2027, not $65,000–$70,000.

qualification.reason: The June 30 checkpoint has a number (500 members), a trigger (below 400) and a consequence (options including sponsorship), all checkable, though the figures are still in brackets.

objections.reason: It deals with the 11-year colleague and invites the sales-minded members to help, but it skips their most likely question, why not keep ads while building membership, and the plan for the colleague is still a placeholder.

fit.reason: It is a tightly organised one-page board memo that ends with a numbered list of what the board is asked to approve, as the brief requested.
